question.:question/problem: Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=\frac{2}{- x + y}$ along the curve $C$ parametrized by $r(t)=⟨- 4 t,\,- 4 t - 2⟩$ for $t\in [1,5].$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To calculate the line integral, we will use the formula

$$
\int_C f(x,y)\,\text{d}s=\int_a^b f(r(t))\,\|r^{\prime}(t)\|\,\text{d}t.
$$

Since $r(t)=⟨- 4 t,\,- 4 t - 2⟩,$ then along the curve we have $x=- 4 t$ and $y=- 4 t - 2.$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t)$ and $\|r^{\prime}(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}j \\ &=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 4 t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 4 t - 2)j \\ &=(-4)i+(-4)j \\ \|r^{\prime}(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})^2+(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})^2} \\ &=\sqrt{(-4)^2+(-4)^2} \\ &=\sqrt{32} \\ &=4 \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if $f(x,y)=\frac{2}{- x + y}$, then we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t))&=\frac{2}{(- 4 t - 2)-(- 4 t)} \\ &=\frac{2}{-2} \\ &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C \frac{2}{- x + y}\,\text{d}s&=\int_{1}^{5}f(r(t))\|r^{\prime}(t)\|\,\text{d}t \\ &=\int_{1}^{5}(-1)\cdot (4 \sqrt{2})\,\text{d}t \\ &=(4 \sqrt{2})\int_{1}^{5}-1\,\text{d}t \\ &=\int_{1}^{5}- 4 \sqrt{2}\,\text{d}t \\ &=(- 4 \sqrt{2})\left[t\right]_{1}^{5} \\ &=\left[(- 4 \sqrt{2} t)\right]_{1}^{5} \\ &=\left((- 4 \sqrt{2} (5))\right)-\left((- 4 \sqrt{2} (1))\right) \\ &=\left((- 20 \sqrt{2})\right)-\left((- 4 \sqrt{2})\right) \\ &=- 16 \sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
